channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Midterm elections updates: Trump says he'll be 'Mr. Veto' if Dems control Congress
item.description: President Donald Trump is scheduled to appear at the Reflecting Pool on Monday.

item.title: European grocery chains' freezers, refrigerators targeted in apparent cyberattacks
item.description: Temperature settings were increased, resulting in food spoilage, companies said.

item.title: Iran engages US in 'intensive' negotiations to avert fresh war outbreak
item.description: Tehran on Monday said that the country was holding "intensive" indirect talks with Washington to avoid a fresh round of US attacks on Iran ahead of the US midterm elections this week. Foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei shared Iranian plans to reopen blockaded energy corridor, the Strait of Hormuz, if the US were to meet its demands.

item.title: Iran offers deal on Hormuz Strait, Netanyahu wants to 'finish the job'
item.description: Iran said Monday it had a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks with the United States, shortening a process originally expected to take seven days. Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he wanted to "finish the job" first. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley has more.

item.title: Petition to ban French right-wing TV channel clears 500,000 signatures after racist killing
item.description: A petition calling for right-wing television channel CNews to be taken off-air cleared half a million signatures on Monday after a Frenchman shot and killed a French national of Congolese origin and wounded seven others. The 39-year-old shooter is believed to have been an avid watcher of CNews, which is owned by ultra-conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré and has been accused of promoting far-right anti-immigrant views.

item.title: British adventurer arrives back at mother's home after 28-year journey
item.description: British adventurer Karl Bushby enjoyed an emotional reunion with his mother and family on Monday, as he arrived back home after a 28-year, 50,000-kilometre trek from South America, crossing four continents on foot.

item.title: DOJ asks for Supreme Court to intervene on California ballot demands
item.description: On the eve of the Nov. 3 election, the Trump administration is hoping the Supreme Court will reverse lower courts that rejected its request to order California to set aside the ballots of thousands of people it says are "likely" noncitizens.

item.title: What changes if Democrats win a majority in Congress?
item.description: Americans head to the polls on Tuesday for the US midterm elections, which could flip the majority in one or both houses of Congress from the Republicans to the Democrats. What would a Democratic majority mean for the country's political landscape, and how might Democrats move to keep President Donald Trump in check?

item.title: WATCH: Seahawks inspire young leaders beyond the field
item.description: ABC News' Kayna Whitworth reports live from Lumen Field in Seattle on how the Seahawks are helping kids build leadership skills and pursue their dreams.

item.title: Judge dismisses DOJ case against two ex-FBI agents who investigated Hunter Biden
item.description: A judge has dismissed the DOJ's federal false statements case against two former FBI agents accused of lying to Congress about past investigations of Hunter Biden.

item.title: A musical overview of trans-European punk
item.description: This week on arts24, we're bringing you a double dose of European punk. Elias Bender Rønnenfelt is a singer with Copenhagen's finest post-punk export, Iceage. The group is currently touring Europe, and he is stopping off in Paris this week to play the Pitchfork festival solo. We also welcome Chris Hughes from Fat Dog. Born in South London in 2020 during lockdown, Fat Dog have just released their second album "Cancel Me (I'm Tired)", which will thrill synth lovers and punk rockers alike. They are currently touring France and Europe.

item.title: Israel's president begins process of coalition government negotiations
item.description: Israel's President Isaac Herzog begins the process of coalition government negotiations this week. One possibility is for the centrist opposition bloc to form a government with the Arab parties, which would oust current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Protests for and against such a coalition this weekend made it clear the Israeli public is divided over the idea.

item.title: Scientists begin tests on human composting, an eco-friendly alternative to burials and cremation
item.description: Humans have caused irreversible changes to our planet in their time on Earth, pollution that continues even in death. Cremation relies heavily on fossil fuels, while traditional burials take up land. So is there a more eco-friendly way to honour our loved ones? French scientists are exploring the possibility of composting human bodies, a process that returns those who have died to the earth. Our Down to Earth team reports.

item.title: Nine dead in small plane crash near Trump's Florida home
item.description: Nine people were killed Sunday when the Learjet they were travelling in plummeted into a neighbourhood in southern Florida, just miles from US President Donald Trump's resort home of Mar-a-Lago, officials said.

item.title: Inflation, war and corruption: Will anger at Trump see Republicans punished at midterms?
item.description: Donald Trump and his Republican Party will make last-gasp pitches to US midterm voters Monday to hold back a predicted Democrat wave that could take over Congress and impose tight political constraints on the president for the first time in two years. With Trump's popularity at an historic low, many are predicting voters will punish the Republican Party at the polls. France 24's Philip Turle takes a closer look.

item.title: Heading into the midterms, 'no US president in recent times has been as unpopular as Donald Trump'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics at Queen Mary University of London. He says that "Donald Trump is damaged goods at this point in his presidency." With this uncompromising assessment, Johnson takes us through the political forces shaping the 2026 US midterm elections. Far from assuming that Trump's formidable campaigning instincts can once again mobilize Republican voters, Johnson questions whether the president's political influence has become a liability for the very party he once transformed. He points to a potentially significant realignment within the American electorate. Economic grievances, rising living costs, trade disputes and disillusionment with the war in Iran appear, in Johnson's reading, to be weakening important elements of the coalition that sustained Trump's return to power. item.title: WATCH: Video of ICE agent apparently pointing gun in bystander's face during arrest
item.description: ICE is facing new scrutiny over a video that allegedly shows an ICE agent pointing a gun in the face of a bystander in California.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia report fake emergency alerts after cyberattacks target apps
item.description: Authorities in Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert mobile apps had been targeted by cyberattacks, with users in Ukraine receiving false warnings of an imminent nuclear threat. Moscow said that hackers had sent fake emergency alerts after gaining access to the Russian Emergency Situations Ministry’s mobile app, and that efforts were ongoing to restore the app's functionality.

item.title: US Midterms: Will Gen Z enthusiasm help turn Michigan Senate blue?
item.description: Michigan’s Senate seat is a must-win for the Democratic Party as it seeks to take control of the upper house of Congress. There’s a surge of energy behind progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed, especially among younger voters. But can Gen Z's enthusiasm translate into votes and help Democrats win a critical Senate seat?

item.title: Democratic Rep. Stevens endorses GOP candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan US Senate race
item.description: Stevens and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed have feuded publicly recently over a campaign ad Stevens said was anti-Semitic.

item.title: Man who stabbed 10 on train said 'I am the baddest', court hears
item.description: A man who stabbed 10 people on a train said "I am the baddest, no-one is as bad as me" as he paced up and down on a different train the day before, a court has heard.

item.title: Could Argentina’s Patagonia become a haven for data centres?
item.description: Around the world, citizens and lawmakers are increasingly pushing back against the construction of data centres, citing noise pollution, massive power consumption and general unsightliness. But Argentina's President Javier Milei wants more of them - and the government thinks it may have found an ideal location, in the vast open steppes of Patagonia.

item.title: French school protests resume on smaller scale after autumn break
item.description: French high school student protests resumed on Monday on a ​much smaller scale than in past weeks as pupils returned from a two-week break, with youngsters trying to blockade a few high schools in Paris, Marseille and Rennes.

item.title: Sour grapes? Dems shocked as Haley Stevens breaks ranks
item.description: France 24’s Fraser Jackson takes a look at the state of play one day ahead of crucial midterm elections in the US as both Democrats and Republicans make their final bids for votes. Meanwhile, Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens has rocked the state’s Senate race by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed. Stevens lost the Michigan Democrats' Senate primary to El-Sayed in a bitterly contested race, leading some to accuse her of sour grapes.

item.title: WATCH: A look at the state of the midterm races
item.description: ABC News' Senior Political Correspondent Rachel Scott breaks down the state of play as a new New York Times/Siena poll shows Democrats are gaining ground, slightly pulling ahead in key Senate races.

item.title: Fresh wave of fridge cyberattacks hits European supermarkets
item.description: Stores and supermarkets across Belgium, Luxembourg, Finland, Estonia and Sweden all reported early Monday abrupt temperature spikes in their fridges and freezers in an apparent cyberattack targeting refrigeration units. The incidents follow a similar attack that hit hundreds of supermarkets across France in October, triggering food loss and fires.

item.title: Greenpeace deploys boulders in North Sea to 'protect porpoises'
item.description: Greenpeace says it has formed an underwater barrier with boulders in the North Sea to prevent "destructive fishing" in an area created to protect porpoises.

item.title: Italian journalists under police protection as threats rise across the country
item.description: Italy is the European country with the largest number of journalists under police protection. There, journalism is a profession particularly susceptible to threats and intimidation, but the European Union's measures to protect press freedom are slow to be implemented. FRANCE 24's team has more.

item.title: US midterm elections: North Carolina farmers hit hard by inflation
item.description: On the eve of the midterm elections, US President Donald Trump's unpopularity is impacting Republicans across the board. Many states with seats once considered Republican strongholds are now on shaky ground. One of them is North Carolina, a rural state where one in five jobs is tied to agriculture.

item.title: Michigan Democrat's endorsement of Republican ruffles critical Senate race
item.description: A prominent Michigan Democrat endorsed Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday, giving President Donald Trump's Republicans an unexpected boost in a critical US Senate race two days before midterm elections that will decide control of Congress.

item.title: 'No political solution' to anger in France, expert says amid ongoing protests
item.description: With the vast majority of French high schools reopening despite calls for new blockades, and the number of people attending weekend demonstrations down for the third week in a row, are the protests in France beginning to die out? We spoke to one political expert who says he believes they will, saying it is difficult to see who people are protesting against, given that the government has no majority in parliament.

item.title: WATCH: Sisters go from lifesaving surgery to running a marathon
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to cancer survivor Kate Stevens, who received a bone marrow transplant from her sister and, around two decades later, ran a marathon with her.

item.title: How Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion
item.description: A tearful Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion at 20 years and 68 ​days old on Sunday when he finished third for Mercedes in a red-flagged and restarted Mexico City Grand Prix won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

item.title: US Midterms: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens defects from party
item.description: Democrats sought on Monday, November 2, to contain a rift in Michigan's US Senate race after one of their own crossed party lines to endorse the Republican candidate, as both parties made final pitches before midterm elections that will decide control of Congress. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.

item.title: 'More patients and fewer doctors': The struggle for maternity care in Afghanistan
item.description: Afghanistan has one of the highest maternal mortality rates in the world. Experts say on average, a woman dies every two hours from complications during childbirth. The problem has become more accute since the Taliban returned to power in 2021, with access to healthcare for Afghan women becoming increasingly difficult. FRANCE 24's team reports from on the ground.

item.title: Two economists studied California's billionaire tax. They reached wildly different conclusions
item.description: What happens in California could shape how America taxes the superrich. But will its billionaire tax fill state coffers — or drain them?

item.title: 'Everything is destroyed': Hackers target refrigerators in new cyber attacks
item.description: Cyber hackers have targeted fridges and freezers in supermarkets in several European countries including Ireland – causing temperatures to increase and food to spoil.

item.title: Man jailed for life after dragging headteacher to his death under his car
item.description: A man who hit a cyclist and knowingly dragged him for more than a mile under his car has been sentenced to at least 25 years in prison for the murder.

item.title: With students scarce, college admissions offices get friendlier, less intimidating
item.description: Colleges are trying to transform an admissions process that has often been daunting, secretive and stressful into an experience that's open, easier — and downright friendly.

item.title: How does this fluoride-free toothpaste compare when it comes to oral health?
item.description: Many people are swapping out their fluoride dental products for ones made with a mineral called hydroxyapatite. What do dentists say about it?

item.title: What Vance's midterm push reveals about his potential 2028 bid
item.description: Vance's delivery is different from the president's but his speeches contain plenty of MAGA DNA.

item.title: UN's peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years
item.description: The U.N.'s long-running peacekeeping mission for the disputed Western Sahara ceased operations Sunday after 35 years. Once ruled by Spain, it is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front.

item.title: WATCH: Thrilling finishes at NYC marathon
item.description: Sweden's Andreas Almgren won his first men's NYC marathon, and Kenya's Shelia Chepkirui won her second NYC marathon.

item.title: British backpackers in Australia could face changes to visa rules
item.description: British backpackers in Australia could be forced to spend more time in regional areas under proposed changes to the country's working holiday visa.

item.title: Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after suffering a stroke, chief of staff says
item.description: U.S. Sen. Chris Murphy has been hospitalized after suffering a stroke, his chief of staff said in a statement on Sunday.

item.title: DOJ urges sanctions for database analysis critical of its noncitizen voting claims
item.description: The Justice Department is urging a federal judge to consider whether to hold an immigrant rights group in contempt of court for disclosing the results of its analysis of a dataset of alleged noncitizens registered to vote in California

item.title: Pilot's last words before jet crashes in Florida, killing all nine on board
item.description: A business jet has crashed in a Florida neighbourhood killing all nine people on board.

item.title: Suspected far-right activists from Britain 'with tear gas bombs' detained in France
item.description: Five suspected far-right activists from Britain were detained in northern France last Thursday, according to authorities.

item.title: Former Ireland European 1,500m champion dies at age of 34
item.description: Former European 1,500m champion Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34.

item.title: WATCH: The volunteers helping get the NYC marathon running
item.description: While the spotlight will be on the nearly 60,000 people running the course, they would not be there without the help of thousands of volunteers on the sidelines.

item.title: The King to speak about slavery with 'unflinching honesty'
item.description: The King will speak about slavery with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" in a speech to Commonwealth leaders amid increasing pressure for Britain to offer an apology over its role in the transatlantic slave trade.

item.title: UN demands investigation into death of staff member in Houthi custody
item.description: A Yemeni staff member of the UN Human Rights Office has died in Houthi custody after being arbitrarily held for more ​than two years, the UN human rights chief has said.

item.title: Election workers describe toll of DOJ threats in court filings
item.description: California election officials described the Trump administration’s legal threats as having consequences on their mental health, according to court papers.

item.title: DC, Virginia file suit to block construction on Trump's proposed arch
item.description: Washington D.C. and Virginia are asking a judge to block the president's Triumphal Arch.

item.title: Judge dismisses Trump's Wall Street Journal lawsuit
item.description: A US judge has dismissed President Donald Trump's lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal over a story about a birthday card he allegedly sent Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Judge says court will investigate government officials in DC golf course case
item.description: The judge wants to know if lawyers tried to mislead her over Trump's plans.

item.title: Majority of funds stolen in cryptocurrency hack replenished, Binance says
item.description: Around 90% of stolen cryptocurrency assets following a hack on a major exchange has been replenished, according to Binance.

item.title: Man dies and another injured after attack at centre housing migrants
item.description: A man has died following an attack at a centre housing migrants in Ireland.

item.title: WATCH: Suspected sailboat thief killed in Rhode Island police shootout
item.description: Body camera footage shows the dramatic police shootout that left a suspected sailboat thief dead in Newport, Rhode Island. The 40-foot boat was stolen back in August.

item.title: These House races could determine which party is in control in the next Congress
item.description: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are on the ballot when voters head to the polls on Nov. 3.

item.title: DOJ says election officials could face jail time if they fail to preserve records
item.description: The DOJ has warned election officials in multiple states that they could face jail time if they fail to preserve election records in accordance with federal law.

item.title: WATCH: How to keep pets safe on Halloween
item.description: Experts say some candy can contain ingredients that owners may not know are dangerous. Dr. Gary Richter, veterinarian and founder of "Ultimate Pet Nutrition," shares more pet safety tips.

item.title: WATCH: Baby loons play with their moms in must-see video
item.description: You can see more about the baby loons and other animals on "Inside the Enchanted Waterways" on Disney+.

item.title: States push back on Trump's noncitizen voting claims
item.description: The Trump administration has warned several states that their voter rolls include noncitizens, but many of those claims haven't held up to scrutiny.

item.title: WATCH: What we know about Binance security breach
item.description: Dave Merkel, co-founder and CEO of cybersecurity company Expel, talks about the major breach.

item.title: WATCH: Remembering Patrick Stewart in his own words
item.description: As tributes pour in for Sir Patrick Stewart, World News Tonight remembers his interview with Diane Sawyer – sharing how theater became his safe space and his home.

item.title: WATCH: See National Geographic's best destinations for 2026
item.description: ABC News' Sam Champion highlights some of the must-visit places featured on National Geographic's annual list of the world's best travel destinations.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events
